specification_compliance: The working-tree copy of addons/media_import/backend/service.py:46-55 and subscription/manager.py:101-108 limits a sanitized title to 200 characters and 200 UTF-8 bytes. It applies NFC first, then truncates to the byte limit with decode('utf-8','ignore') so no partial multibyte character is left, then strips trailing combining marks. The decisions.md record of an in-app run and a pre-fix control matches this behavior.
Headroom check: a 200-byte stem, plus ' (n)' and a sidecar suffix such as '.stt_temp.<ext>.part', stays under the 255-byte name limit on Linux file systems for any realistic n and extension.
potential_unspecified_behavior: After the byte cut, the code strips trailing combining marks but not other trailing characters. A cut can therefore leave a trailing space or '.', which the earlier strip('. ') would have removed. This is cosmetic only on Linux file systems.
regression_risks: The two sanitizers are duplicated, one in service.py and one in subscription/manager.py, so they can drift apart. tests/test_nfc_names.py checks that both return the same name, which limits this risk.
The subscription-driven import path was not exercised in the app, as decisions.md acknowledges.
test_coverage: addons/media_import/backend/tests/test_nfc_names.py:51-74 covers the byte cut ('あ'*100 -> 'あ'*66), NFD input that is truncated after NFC, and the assertion len(encode()) <= 200, for both sanitizers.
